rules: The current HM Land Registry INSPIRE Index Polygons download page says the dataset was published on 5 July 2026.
HM Land Registry states that new INSPIRE Index Polygon files are published on the first Sunday of every month.
HM Land Registry states that the current INSPIRE files remain accessible until the next update replaces them.
HM Land Registry lists INSPIRE polygon downloads by local-authority area.
HM Land Registry states that GIS software is needed to view downloaded INSPIRE Index Polygons.
Downloading the INSPIRE files is subject to the Open Government Licence conditions of use.
The current July 2026 INSPIRE download index lists London Borough of Barnet.
The current July 2026 INSPIRE download index lists London Borough of Enfield.
HM Land Registry publishes the local-authority INSPIRE files as GML.
HM Land Registry projection guidance identifies British National Grid as EPSG:27700 and warns BNG-to-WGS84 conversion can shift some features by up to 15 metres.
The current Planning Data documentation says the API provides access to more than 100 planning and housing datasets for England.
A coordinate query uses latitude and longitude to return entities whose geometry intersects the constructed point.
Planning Data allows multiple dataset parameters in one coordinate query.
Planning Data recommends UPRN search through q as more precise than a coordinate for registered properties.
Planning Data entity results can include name, dataset, start-date, geometry and point fields.
Planning Data warns that an empty result does not prove that no planning constraints exist because coverage varies by area.
The documentation example retrieves 337 local planning authorities in one request.
Raw spatial searches accept WKT geometry and Planning Data states those coordinates should use WGS84 EPSG:4326.
Planning Data supports geometry relations including within, intersects, contains, covers, overlaps and crosses.
Planning Data documents offset pagination, no portfolio batch endpoint, polite per-property rate limiting, and bulk downloads with local spatial intersections for large portfolios.
The current Environment Agency DTM 1m record describes a raster elevation model covering about 99 percent of England at 1 metre spatial resolution.
The DTM uses the last or only laser return and removes surface objects to model terrain.
The current DTM 1m record describes a composite produced in 2022 from archive and National LIDAR Programme surveys.
The 2022 composite contains source surveys undertaken between 6 June 2000 and 2 April 2022.
The DTM 1m data is available as GeoTIFF rasters in 5km tiles aligned to the OS National Grid.
The DTM 1m data is presented in metres relative to Ordnance Survey Newlyn using the OSTN15 transformation method.
The Environment Agency states individual input LIDAR surveys have vertical accuracy of plus or minus 15 centimetres RMSE.
The DTM 1m coordinate reference system is EPSG:27700 and the record is licensed under the Open Government Licence.
Defra documents persistent LIDAR Composite WCS endpoints using WCS 2.0.1 and says WCS returns raw pixel values such as elevation.
The separate Coverage Metadata - Survey Data record is published by the Environment Agency and exposes WMS, WFS and OGC API Features service links.
The current OS Data Hub download page shows OS Terrain 50 with Version Date July 2026.
Ordnance Survey describes OS Terrain 50 as a low-resolution digital terrain model for Great Britain with 50 metre post spacing.
Current OS Terrain 50 documentation states the product is updated annually in July.
OS Terrain 50 grid and contour data are supplied as 10km-by-10km tiles identified from the National Grid reference of the south-west corner.
OS Terrain 50 is Open Data and is free to view, download and use for commercial, educational and personal purposes.
OS Terrain 50 product supply documentation states the tiled national dataset contains 2,858 10km tiles arranged into 55 100km grid-square folders.
OS Terrain 50 product supply documentation states the full national grid supply is approximately 157 MB compressed.
OS Terrain 50 metadata identifies British National Grid EPSG:27700 and Ordnance Datum Newlyn EPSG:5701.
OS Terrain 50 supply documentation says online download is available with no registration required.
The OS Downloads API documentation says it can discover OpenData products and product metadata and automate downloads; the current Terrain 50 Data Hub page confirms free OpenData download access.
